#| label: loss
"Residual F(u, θ) = A u + u³ − θ with zero Dirichlet ends, written into F."
function residual!(F, u, θ)
    n = length(u)
    ih2 = (n + 1)^2
    for i in 1:n
        l = i > 1 ? u[i-1] : zero(eltype(u))
        r = i < n ? u[i+1] : zero(eltype(u))
        F[i] = ih2 * (2u[i] - l - r) + u[i]^3 - θ[i]
    end
end

"Solve J δ = F in place (δ overwrites F), J = A + 3 diag(u²): the Thomas algorithm."
function thomas!(F, c, u)
    n = length(u)
    ih2 = (n + 1)^2
    off = -ih2
    b = 2ih2 + 3u[1]^2
    c[1] = off / b
    F[1] = F[1] / b
    for i in 2:n                                  # forward elimination
        b = 2ih2 + 3u[i]^2 - off * c[i-1]
        c[i] = off / b
        F[i] = (F[i] - off * F[i-1]) / b
    end
    for i in n-1:-1:1                             # back substitution
        F[i] -= c[i] * F[i+1]
    end
end

"Newton until the step is small; returns the solution and the iteration count."
function newton_solve(θ::AbstractVector{T}) where {T}
    n = length(θ)
    u, F, c = zeros(T, n), zeros(T, n), zeros(T, n)
    it, converged = 0, false
    while !converged && it < MAXITER              # data-dependent trip count
        residual!(F, u, θ)
        thomas!(F, c, u)                          # F now holds the Newton step δ
        u .-= F
        it += 1
        converged = maximum(abs, F) <= TOL * maximum(abs, u)
    end
    return u, it
end

newton_loss(θ, uobs) = sum(abs2, first(newton_solve(θ)) .- uobs)

#| label: grad
"Reverse mode straight through the while loop, the Newton steps and the Thomas sweeps."
function newton_gradient(θ, uobs)
    dθ = zero(θ)
    Enzyme.autodiff(Reverse, newton_loss, Active, Duplicated(θ, dθ), Const(uobs))
    return dθ
end

g = newton_gradient(θ0, uobs0)
@printf "Newton iterations: %d   loss = %.12f   ‖∇loss‖ = %.6f\n" last(newton_solve(θ0)) newton_loss(θ0, uobs0) sqrt(sum(abs2, g))

#| label: grad-implicit
# The alternative a numerical analyst would choose: at the solution, F(u*, θ) = 0, so
# dL/dθ = λ with Jᵀλ = ∂L/∂u (J is symmetric here). One tridiagonal solve, no tape.
function newton_gradient_implicit(θ, uobs)
    u, _ = newton_solve(θ)
    λ, c = 2 .* (u .- uobs), similar(u)
    thomas!(λ, c, u)
    return λ
end

g_imp = newton_gradient_implicit(θ0, uobs0)
@printf "unrolled vs implicit: max rel. difference %.1e\n" maximum(abs, g - g_imp) / maximum(abs, g)

#| label: bench
ns = [10^3, 10^4, 10^5, 10^6]
records = []
for variant in ("unrolled", "implicit"), (k, n) in enumerate(ns)
    θ, uobs = inputs(n)
    grad = variant == "unrolled" ? newton_gradient : newton_gradient_implicit
    compile_s = k == 1 ? @elapsed(grad(θ, uobs)) : nothing
    samples = n >= 10^5 ? 3 : 10
    push!(records, (; dtype="Float64", variant, N=n, iterations=last(newton_solve(θ)),
        forward_s = time_median(() -> newton_loss(θ, uobs); samples),
        grad_s    = time_median(() -> grad(θ, uobs); samples),
        compile_s, peak_mem_bytes = @allocated(grad(θ, uobs))))
end
write_results(EXAMPLE, "enzyme", "cpu", records)
for r in records
    @printf "%-9s n=%-8d iterations %2d   forward %9.3f ms   gradient %9.3f ms   allocated %8.1f MiB\n" r.variant r.N r.iterations 1e3r.forward_s 1e3r.grad_s r.peak_mem_bytes / 2^20
end
